body.p: Pulling and pushing is one of the most common git workflows. If you are unfamiliar with it, go to the git website.
After you commit changes to a local repository, use Push to make them available in the remote repository.
Use Pull to bring other people's commits from the remote repository into your local repository.
In the Pull drop-down menu, you can choose between Pull (merge) and Pull (rebase). The action you choose becomes the default action of the toolbar button.
Use Pull... when you need to pull from a remote branch other than the tracked branch.
body.note: When you push a local branch that does not have a corresponding remote branch, a remote branch with the same name is created automatically.

section.title: Pushing commits
section.p: Push commits to add changes to a repository's current branch. The repository can be local or remote.
Use push to commit changes to the current branch and create a record of those changes with a commit message.
If your local branch is associated with a remote branch, pull changes or verify that the branches have not diverged before pushing your changes to avoid file conflicts.

section.title: Pulling commits
section.p: Pull commits to bring your local branch up to date with its associated remote branch.
